cases.purpose: Reject extra fields and embedded NUL bytes without damaging subsequent lookups; distinguish a directory read failure from an empty database.
cases.oracle: Seven colon-separated passwd fields; physical rows with embedded NUL or extra fields are malformed. Directory reads fail.
cases.comparison: Exact status and diagnostic class for each lookup, with the shell still alive.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t su) == builtin ]] || exit 99
export BASHPASSWD_KERNEL_SECRETS=0 PHCLIB_PASSWD=rows
printf 'extra:x:1:1::/:/bin/sh:tail\nother:x:1:1::/:/bin/sh:tail\nnul:x:1:1::/:/bin/sh\0:tail\nshort:x:1:1::/\n' > rows
try() {
  local label=$1 user=$2 rc e c
  su "$user" >out 2>err; rc=$?
  e=$(<err); c=other
  case $e in *"no such user: "*) c=absent;; *"cannot read passwd database"*) c=unreadable;; esac
  [[ ! -s out ]] || c=unexpected-stdout
  printf '%s rc=%d diag=%s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$c"
}
try extra extra
try nul nul
try short short
try absent absent
/usr/bin/mkdir dbdir
PHCLIB_PASSWD=dbdir; try directory absent
: > empty; PHCLIB_PASSWD=empty; try empty absent
printf 'shell=alive\n'
/usr/bin/rm -rf rows out err dbdir empty
cases.stdout:
extra rc=1 diag=absent
nul rc=1 diag=absent
short rc=1 diag=absent
absent rc=1 diag=absent
directory rc=1 diag=unreadable
empty rc=1 diag=absent
shell=alive
